title: Reject a snapshot with six planted defects

blocks.text: A water utility's planning tool exports a main-replacement snapshot each cycle, and this cycle's export has six defects planted in it. Your gate must reject it, and find all six.

Each job $`j`$ has a cost profile $`c_{j,0}, c_{j,1}, \dots`$ (one entry per year of work, $k), a window $`e_j \le t \le l_j`$ of start years, a `required` flag, and possibly a prerequisite $`a(j)`$ with a lag $`L_j`$: job $`j`$ may start in year $`t`$ only if $`a(j)`$ started in a year $`s \le t - L_j`$. Each year $`y`$ of the horizon $`H`$ has a budget $`B_y`$. The model has $`x_{j,t} \in \{0, 1\}`$ for each start year $`t \in T_j`$, where $`T_j`$ holds the window's years whose whole work falls inside the horizon: the snapshot's `horizon` is a list of consecutive years, and $`t`$ is in $`T_j`$ when $`e_j \le t \le l_j`$, $`t`$ is at least the horizon's first year, and $`t + |c_j| - 1`$ (the job's last year of work) is at most the horizon's last year. The rows are
In `review.py`, write `starts` (the set $`T_j`$) and the five rules, and `review(snapshot, previous)`, which returns every finding as `(severity, rule, subject)`, sorted. `rejected` is written.

rows: the jobs on the cycle, sorted, joined with `+`
following prerequisites from a job leads back to it
no start of its prerequisite plus the lag reaches any of its own starts
a required job has no start year
what every plan must pay for costs more than all budgets together
a year's budget is more than 3 times, or less than a third of, its amount in `previous`

blocks.text: Give `prerequisite-too-late` the severity the lesson's rule calls for: an error when the finding proves no plan exists, a warning otherwise. The finding proves it when the job must be done in every plan: the job is required, or it is the prerequisite (directly or through a chain of `after`) of a required job. A job that is optional and needed by no required job can simply be left out, so its finding is a warning. The same set of must-do jobs is what `required-over-budget` adds up. With no `previous`, there is no drift.

The six planted defects are one of each: a prerequisite cycle, a too-late prerequisite on a job every plan must do, a too-late prerequisite on an optional job, a required job with no start year, required spending above all budgets together, and a budget that drifted from `previous`. The main test checks that `review` finds each of them. About forty lines.

cases.says: a clean snapshot gets no finding, and the export with six planted defects is rejected with all six found
a cycle of prerequisites is one finding, not one per job on it
a required job whose prerequisite cannot start early enough proves there is no plan
the same problem on an optional job leaves a plan, so it only warns
a job not flagged required but needed by a required job must be done, so its too-late prerequisite is an error
a start year counts only if every year of the job's work falls inside the horizon
a prerequisite of a required job must be paid for too
a budget that grew or shrank by more than the factor is flagged; a 30% cut is not

origin.section: Severity Follows What a Finding Proves: Errors Block, Warnings Report

concepts: a gate that runs every rule on a snapshot, compares it with the last accepted one, and gives each finding the severity of what it proves
